items.title: Chevron Stock Is Near a Record High. Here’s Why the Rally May Not Be Over
items.summary: Chevron's stock has surged over 42% this year, nearing a record high, but 24/7 Wall St. maintains a "Hold" recommendation with a target implying slight downside. While strong Q2 FY26 results, operational efficiencies, and a significant power purchase agreement with Microsoft present a bullish case, the stock's high P/E ratio compared to peers and potential oil price fluctuations suggest caution. The long-term projections depend on continued execution and market conditions.

items.title: Freeport-McMoRan shares surge as copper hits record $14,694/ton
items.summary: Freeport-McMoRan shares surged after copper hit a new all-time high of $14,694 per ton on the LME, driven by supply pressures including accelerated US-bound metal flows and reduced production from Chile. This price surge significantly boosts Freeport-McMoRan's potential EBITDA, with management projecting higher earnings at elevated copper prices. The copper rally's continuation hinges on upcoming economic data, specifically the European Central Bank meeting and US inflation figures.

items.title: Franco-Nevada Corporation (FNV): Why the Gold Royalty Major Is Back in Focus After Record First-Half Results
items.summary: Franco-Nevada Corporation (FNV) is gaining investor attention after reporting record first-half 2026 financial results, driven by strong precious metal and oil prices. The company operates a unique royalty and streaming business model, providing diversified exposure to gold and other commodities without the direct costs and risks of mining. With a debt-free balance sheet, significant capital for acquisitions, and a history of dividend increases, FNV offers a lower-risk investment in the precious metals sector, despite its premium valuation.

items.title: NextEra secures $1.9B DOE loan for Duane Arnold nuclear restart
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Energy has finalized a $1.9 billion loan to NextEra Energy to restart the 615-MW Duane Arnold nuclear facility in Iowa, which ceased operations in 2020. The plant is expected to restart by 2029 and Google will be its primary customer, using the output to power its data centers. This initiative highlights a growing trend of restarting nuclear plants to meet the escalating electricity demand from data centers.

items.title: CoStar: Canada’s retail market still recovering from Hudson’s Bay stores closing
items.summary: Canada's retail market is still recovering from the closure of Hudson's Bay stores in 2025, which caused a significant jump in mall and overall retail vacancy rates. The vacancy rate is expected to remain steady at around 2.5% over the next year, with construction activity at a decade low. Rent growth has decelerated and is projected to bottom out around 0% by Q2 2027 before recovering.

items.title: Wynn Resorts stock rises on a strike at Encore Boston Harbor
items.summary: Wynn Resorts stock has risen to USD 91.54 despite over 1,300 union workers striking at its Encore Boston Harbor property, with no new bargaining sessions scheduled. The strike, centered on wage and benefit disputes, is seen as a key company-specific catalyst, even as the stock trades below its 52-week low but maintains a consensus target of USD 133.82. The company's Q2 earnings showed EPS of USD 1.24, exceeding estimates, and revenue grew 6.9% year-over-year, providing a positive operational backdrop amidst the labor dispute.

items.title: Taylor Swift Promoter Says Live Nation Shut Him Out as AEG Calls for Ticketmaster Breakup
items.summary: Both AEG and veteran promoter Louis Messina are urging a federal judge to reject the Justice Department's proposed settlement with Live Nation and Ticketmaster, arguing it fails to curb the company's power. Messina alleges Live Nation effectively shut him out of its amphitheaters in 2024, preventing artists from using him as their promoter. AEG contends the settlement preserves Ticketmaster's dominance by maintaining incentives for venues to use their services, arguing that structural changes, such as separating Ticketmaster from Live Nation, are necessary.
